$comment: The single source for every colour in the product (UX spec § Design System).
The rule this file exists to enforce: a colour is never written twice. The
component ships CSS custom properties and the console uses Tailwind, and two
hand-maintained palettes drift — so both are generated from here and CI fails if
the generated files are stale (R-013).
Tokens are semantic, never literal: state.recorded, not green. The point of the
token is that it survives a change of mind about the colour.
The two themes are the two ways a drawing is reproduced. Light is the positive:
india ink on warm bond, the sheet laid on a slightly darker field. Dark is the
blueprint negative: drawn line in pale cyan-white on a blue-black ground. They are
not an inversion of each other, because a blueprint is not an inverted drawing.
state.refused is carmine in both, and carmine appears nowhere else: on a drawing
sheet the red ink marks the one thing under examination, and in this product the
thing under examination is always what was refused or is not built.
text.fg-terminal is the same in both themes on purpose: the terminal ground is dark
in either, so text on it is light in either. Using text.fg there instead put dark
text on a dark ground in the light theme — invisible, and only in replay.
The terminal group is deliberately untouched by the 2026 redesign. Sixteen ANSI
colours are functional output, not decoration: they were tuned against bg-terminal
and re-tuning them to match a new chrome would trade real legibility for a look.
